stories.title: UK updates climate disclosure rules
stories.summary: The UK Financial Conduct Authority has replaced its climate disclosure requirements with the broader UK Sustainability Reporting Standards. Companies now face a comply or explain approach for general and climate-related disclosures. The regulator previously proposed mandatory climate reporting, but has opted for a more flexible path.

stories.title: EU simplifies sustainability reporting standards
stories.summary: Revised EU sustainability reporting standards entered into force this week, reducing mandatory data points by more than 60 percent. The rules become mandatory for the 2027 financial year, though companies may apply them early for 2026. Reporting now comes with additional flexibility for businesses.

stories.title: ISSB proposes nature-related disclosure framework
stories.summary: The International Sustainability Standards Board has proposed a framework for companies to disclose how their dependence on natural resources affects financial prospects. The board stopped short of introducing a new standard. Chair Emmanuel Faber noted that threats to environmental resources can create risks for company prospects.

stories.title: EBA delays bank reporting requirements
stories.summary: The European Banking Authority will delay new supervisory reporting requirements for EU banks until December 2027. The update includes lighter templates for collateral and stress-testing data, with ESG reporting deferred until 2028. The regulator will publish its final report on the draft standards in December.

stories.title: WBCSD publishes guide on ISSB implementation
stories.summary: The World Business Council for Sustainable Development has released a guide on applying ISSB standards, featuring real-world examples from the first year of mandatory reporting. The publication aims to help companies connect sustainability risks with business strategy and financial performance. Implementation remains a work in progress.

stories.summary: Central Bank of India Wins Excellence Award for ESG Governance at ENQUBE Awards 2026 Central Bank of India has been recognised for ‘Excellence in ESG Governance & Responsible Business’ at the ENQUBE ESG Excellence Awards 2026 held on 29 October 2026 at NSE Auditorium, Mumbai.

stories.title: Korean association gains carbon verification status
stories.summary: The Korean Standards Association is now an accredited verifier for the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. The move is intended to help Korean exporters reduce verification costs and administrative burdens. Previously, companies were required to rely on European verification bodies to meet EU carbon compliance rules.

stories.title: DKSH links loan to climate targets
stories.summary: DKSH has secured a CHF 100 million loan from OCBC with terms tied to emissions targets validated by the Science Based Targets initiative. The financing adds accountability to the company's existing decarbonization plan. The loan has a five-year term.

stories.title: Alternergy plans green bond offering
stories.summary: Alternergy has filed for a shelf registration of up to P10 billion in green bonds with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The company plans an initial P3-billion offering to allow retail investors to participate in its renewable energy projects. The green story is now open to families.

stories.title: CIX launches carbon credit gateway
stories.summary: Climate Impact X has introduced a centralized procurement venue to streamline how companies source international carbon credits eligible under Singapore’s framework. Companies subject to the local carbon tax may use these credits to offset up to 5 percent of their taxable emissions.

stories.title: Verra approves first CCS carbon credits
stories.summary: Verra has approved the first carbon credits under its carbon capture and storage methodology, issued to BKV Corporation for a project in Texas. The project captures carbon dioxide from natural gas processing and stores it underground. The methodology is designed to verify permanent storage of captured emissions.

stories.title: Boomitra delivers 2.6 million soil carbon credits
stories.summary: Boomitra has sold and delivered 2.6 million soil carbon credits from its grassland restoration project in northern Mexico to corporate buyers. CEO Aadith Moorthy described the transaction as the largest delivery of soil carbon credits to date, demonstrating commercial demand for verified soil carbon removal at scale.

stories.title: China raises 6 billion yuan in green bond orders
stories.summary: China attracted over 6 billion yuan in orders for its first yuan-denominated green sovereign bond in Canada, exceeding its 4 billion yuan target. The three- and five-year bonds carry initial yield guidance of 1.8% and 1.9%. The offering aims to connect green financing with economic relations.

stories.title: KOKO Networks collapse serves as market warning
stories.summary: The collapse of Kenya-based KOKO Networks in early 2026 highlights how regulatory uncertainty can threaten climate projects. The company had deployed over 3,000 bioethanol dispensing machines to serve 1.5 million people. Government authorization requirements under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement remain a significant barrier for developers.

stories.title: CalPERS climate solutions portfolio reaches 71 billion dollars
stories.summary: California pension fund CalPERS has reached 71 billion dollars in its climate solutions portfolio. The fund intends to prioritize research into adaptation and resilience while refining the taxonomy used for its climate investments. The transition performance of the assets is reportedly catching up to broader market expectations.

stories.title: Democratic midterm wins may boost COP31 hopes, but Trump still controls US climate policy
stories.summary: Democratic victories in the United States midterm elections could offer encouragement at COP31, but are unlikely to deliver an immediate breakthrough while President Donald Trump continues to direct US climate policy, according to Washington-based observers. stories.title: Nepal calls for Himalayan climate justice at COP31
stories.summary: Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal urged the international community to address climate risks facing the Himalayas during the opening of COP31 in Antalya. Khanal called for concrete global commitments to protect mountain ecosystems and minimize the impacts of climate change on vulnerable regions.

stories.title: World leaders take stage at COP31 but big names missing
stories.summary: World leaders will take the stage at COP31 in Turkiye on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) but some prominent names are missing from this year’s annual UN climate summit even as global warming intensifies. stories.title: Thunberg criticizes COP31 climate negotiations
stories.summary: Climate activist Greta Thunberg condemned the COP31 conference as hypocritical upon her arrival in Antalya. She urged world leaders to prioritize people and the planet over profit, noting that negotiations remain filled with lobbyists from the very industries responsible for the climate crisis.

stories.title: UN chief calls for fossil fuel transition action
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged COP31 co-hosts Turkey and Australia to move from discussing the end of fossil fuels to delivering it. While the hosts are significant fossil fuel exporters, Guterres stated that treating the transition as a taboo subject is no longer acceptable.

stories.title: WMO reports 2026 among warmest years on record
stories.summary: The World Meteorological Organization reports that 2026 is set to be one of the four warmest years on record, with global temperatures 1.47 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. An intensifying El Niño is expected to reach record strength by December, further increasing ocean heat and climate risks.

stories.title: ASA bans ads from four brands over carbon-neutral claims
stories.summary: The ASA has banned advertisements from Who Gives A Crap, ProCook, Grind, and SportsShoes.com. The regulator found the companies presented carbon-neutral or carbon-positive delivery as an environmental benefit without explaining how the status was achieved. Consumers could not distinguish between emission reductions and carbon credit offsets.

stories.title: ISWA World Congress returns to London
stories.summary: The ISWA World Congress 2026 is underway in London, marking its return to the city after 30 years. Hosted by CIWM and the International Solid Waste Association, the event gathers over 1,000 leaders and policymakers to discuss waste management and strategies for turning waste into investable infrastructure.

stories.title: Academics debate AI impact on circularity research
stories.summary: A panel at the ISWA World Congress explored how AI is disrupting scientific research. Dr. Costas Velis noted that large language models like Claude and ChatGPT are changing how waste and circularity science is published. AI is described as the defining technological innovation of our age.

stories.title: Aptar Pharma explores circularity for elastomer waste
stories.summary: Yann Fromont of Aptar Pharma and Clovis Saunier of Moine Recyclage are examining a circular approach to clean elastomer production scrap. By using life cycle assessment insights, the companies aim to keep recovered material in use rather than sending it for incineration as supply chain decarbonisation becomes mandatory.

stories.title: International Recycling Forum 2027 scheduled for April
stories.summary: The 5th International Recycling Forum will take place on 26 and 27 April 2027 in Wiesbaden. Organised by RIGK and EPRO, the conference will focus on translating European legislation and recycling infrastructure requirements into practical solutions for the circular plastics economy. The event will be conducted in English.

stories.title: WRAP campaign targets Christmas food waste
stories.summary: WRAP has launched a campaign titled Make your feast go further. The initiative aims to help consumers save time and money by optimising their Christmas food shopping. The campaign claims that these efforts will prevent food waste during the holiday season.

stories.title: Valorpneu reviews circular economy progress in Portugal
stories.summary: Valorpneu held its 24th Network Meeting in Portugal to discuss the management of used tyres. The event focused on circular economy initiatives, technological innovation, and regulatory changes. Partners reviewed the organisation’s 2026 activities and set strategic priorities for the coming years.

stories.title: Compliance gap emerges in EU packaging rules
stories.summary: Manufacturers preparing for the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation face a significant administrative contrast. While compliance software can generate documentation in minutes, obtaining the required laboratory reports takes approximately six weeks. The process involves technical files, declarations of conformity, and finalising labels.

stories.title: GreenDot acquires 50 percent stake in Léko
stories.summary: GreenDot is acquiring a 50 percent stake in Valorie, the holding company for French producer responsibility organisations Léko and Léko Pro. The move expands GreenDot’s pan-European platform for plastics circularity. CEO Laurent Auguste will lead the new ownership structure following the transaction.

stories.title: Industry calls for PET import safeguards
stories.summary: European PET producers are seeking safeguards against rising imports to protect existing recycling infrastructure. EU Member States have submitted a request to the European Commission, arguing that the industry must protect what already works to build a functional circular economy for food and beverage packaging.

stories.title: COP31 side event addresses zero waste solutions
stories.summary: The United Nations Development Programme hosted a COP31 side event focused on circular economy approaches for climate, nature, and development. The session explored shared zero waste solutions across different waste streams. Full details are unavailable as the server access was restricted.

stories.title: UCM awards projects for circular economy research
stories.summary: The Community of Madrid Circular Economy Chair has awarded seven projects for their contribution to scientific knowledge and sustainability. Winning research includes AI-driven hotel food waste management, metal recovery from photovoltaic cells, and the valorisation of brewer's yeast in food products.

stories.title: Mercedes-Benz delays net-zero target to 2049
stories.summary: Mercedes-Benz has pushed its full carbon neutrality target to 2049, a decade later than its previous 2039 deadline. The company cited a slower-than-expected market for the revision. Investors are now questioning if customer demand can support the company's long-term transformation roadmap.

stories.title: Bloomberg subscription required for electrification analysis
stories.summary: A recent analysis discusses the role of electrification in the global energy transition, suggesting that electric infrastructure remains essential even when powered by coal. The full article and further insights are available to Bloomberg subscribers.

stories.title: Electrification takes priority at COP31
stories.summary: COP31 opened in Antalya with a focus on global electrification. UN climate chief Simon Stiell urged nations to rewire their economies to avoid ongoing fossil fuel cost pain. Turkey and Australia are leading a push to ensure electricity accounts for 35 percent of global energy demand.

stories.title: Global business leaders form electrification alliance
stories.summary: Business leaders have launched the Electric Advantage Leadership Alliance at COP31. The group aims to support the COP Presidency’s drive for global electrification. Further details regarding the alliance's specific commitments are available to subscribers.

stories.title: Levi Strauss appoints new sustainability lead
stories.summary: Levi Strauss and Co has announced the appointment of a new Chief Sustainability Officer. The move follows the company's ongoing efforts to integrate sustainability into its global operations. Further details regarding the appointment are currently inaccessible.

stories.title: Turkey hosts the COP of Implementation
stories.summary: Delegates gather in Antalya from November 9 to 20 for COP31, billed as the COP of Implementation. While the concept sounds simple, organizers expect a full range of complexities. The Turkish presidency aims to meet climate goals by setting measurable targets. Implementation remains a work in progress.

stories.title: COP31 opens in Antalya
stories.summary: Representatives from over 190 countries have arrived in Antalya for the COP31 climate summit. The conference runs through November 20, with Australia leading formal negotiations. Governments face the recurring question of how to fund emissions cuts and protections promised a decade after the Paris Agreement began.

stories.title: Sustainable Carolina publishes 2026 report
stories.summary: Sustainable Carolina released its annual report on October 23, detailing greenhouse gas emissions and campus expansion plans. Authored by Abigail Brewer with contributions from faculty, the document outlines various eco-friendly activities. The university continues to monitor its environmental footprint while the campus grows in size.

stories.title: Research focus at COP31
stories.summary: COP31 has begun in Turkey with an agenda focused on clean energy, waste management, and climate-resilient cities. Researchers are presenting new materials and policies intended to accelerate progress toward global climate targets. The scientific community is currently working on methods to help shape the transition away from fossil fuels.

stories.title: Energy deals take center stage at COP31
stories.summary: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met with six leaders on the sidelines of COP31, including UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres. The meetings coincided with a new electricity agreement between Turkey and Saudi Arabia. Delegates spent the second day navigating crowded transport and working through a program of voluntary energy pledges.

stories.title: Polycab hits 6 GW inverter milestone
stories.summary: Polycab India has reached 6 GW in solar inverter shipments, supplying over 11 lakh units to date. The company claims its products account for 30 percent of rooftop installations under the PM Surya Ghar scheme. It now plans to launch a 500 kW utility-scale inverter next year.
